title: crow account switching and session resume

needs: When the current account runs out of its 5-hour allowance the owner is blocked and cannot do much; crow should offer to continue on another allowed account instead.
Only accounts the owner allows may be used: one is personal, one is shared and must always be confirmed, the others belong to teammates and are never used.
Sessions cut off by a usage limit must be listed and relaunchable on any allowed account, whenever the owner wants.
A handoff must name the exact source conversation: without an id the provider tool takes the newest transcript, which once handed off an automatic retro session instead of the owner's real one.
While no tokens are left the owner should still have something useful to do from the hub.

Whatever crow has learned about the owner (memory) must follow a session to any allowed account; today it sits in one profile's folder and a relaunch on another account starts without it, while the shared account must not end up holding the owner's personal memory.
context: cdx offers `status --json` (5h and weekly usage, block, reset times per account), `can-resume <name>` and `handoff <source> <target> --source-conversation ID`. cdx is not owned by the hub's owner and must stay untouched and unaware of crow.
crow-usage already reads `cdx status --json` for limits; crow-watch already shows agents and usage and can host another view.
Automatic retros run as their own sessions in the same profile and workspace, so a 'newest transcript' lookup picks them up.

A first registry of limit-cut sessions exists at local/state/interrupted-sessions.md (11 sessions on 2026-10-20), built by scanning every profile's transcripts for a final limit message and excluding retros.
Account policy lives in local/context.md today, in prose; it must become machine-readable config in local/.

Memory is per cdx profile (~/.cdx/profiles/<name>/claude-home/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/): main holds 18 files for this project, shared 2, the teammates' accounts none. The private local/ repo is the chosen single source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: An allowed-accounts config in local/ lists each account with a policy (use, ask-first, never); crow never targets an account marked never.
AC2: A scanner builds the interrupted-sessions registry from transcripts (last turn is a limit message, retros and automatic jobs excluded) and is cheap on repeated runs.
AC3: Relaunching a session always passes its conversation id to the handoff and refuses to run without one.
AC4: When the active account is blocked, crow shows the recommended allowed target and asks for confirmation before any handoff; ask-first accounts always require an explicit yes.
AC5: A crow watch view lists interrupted sessions with project, age, size and first prompt, and relaunches the selected one on a chosen allowed account.
AC6: With no usable account, crow offers a no-model mode listing work that needs none (pipeline checks, diff review, registry triage).
AC7: Nothing in the change requires a change to cdx or relies on crow-specific markers inside cdx.

AC8: Memory lives in the private local/ repo and every allowed profile reads it from there while a crow-launched session runs; nothing is copied into a shared account's profile, and writes from any profile land back in local/.

product.title: Keep working when an account runs out
product.overview: crow tracks which accounts the owner may use, notices a blocked account, and relaunches cut-off sessions on an allowed one after confirmation, from a terminal view.
goals: Never lose a session to a usage limit.
Switch accounts with one confirmation and never touch a forbidden one.
Stay useful from the hub when no tokens are left.
non_goals: Using a local model as orchestrator (measured separately first).

backlog_items.title: 1.1 memory in local, shared by every allowed profile
problem: Memory is split per cdx profile, so a session relaunched on another account loses what crow learned, and copying it into a shared account would expose personal notes.
scope_in: Move the cr-0w and per-project memory folders into local/ (its own git history) and point each profile's memory path at them only while a crow-launched session runs.
Write-back so a memory saved from any profile lands in local/ and is committed there.
scope_out: Memory for accounts that are never used.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: after the move the main profile loads the same memories as before, verified by listing them from a session.
AC2: a session launched on the shared account reads the same files from local/ and leaves no copy in its profile once it ends.
AC3: a memory written from any profile appears in local/ and is committed.

backlog_items.title: 1.2 account policy config and interrupted-session registry
problem: Account rules exist only as prose and the registry was built by a one-off script.
scope_in: Machine-readable accounts file in local/ and a bin/ scanner that writes the registry as JSON plus a readable list.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: accounts file with policies is read by one helper used by every crow command.
AC2: the scanner excludes retros and automatic jobs and reuses a cache keyed by file mtime and size.

backlog_items.title: 1.3 guarded relaunch and block detection
problem: A handoff without an id picked the wrong session, and nothing watches for a blocked account.
scope_in: crow command that checks `cdx can-resume`, requires an id and a confirmed allowed target, then runs the handoff; block detection from `cdx status --json`.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the command refuses to run without a conversation id or with a never account.
AC2: an ask-first account needs an explicit yes every time.

backlog_items.title: 1.4 interrupted-sessions view and no-model mode
problem: Relaunching is a manual command and the owner has nothing to do while out of tokens.
scope_in: A crow watch view over the registry with relaunch, and a no-model list of useful work.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the view fills the terminal like the other views and degrades on small terminals.
AC2: selecting a session and an allowed account runs the guarded relaunch.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver account switching and session resume in three steps
plan: 1.1: move memory into local/, wire profile access without copies, verify on main and on the shared account (ask first).
1.2: accounts file, helper and registry scanner with tests.
1.3: guarded relaunch command and block detection; verify with a dry run against cdx.
1.4: crow watch view and no-model mode; render and show the owner before finishing.
